html:
SMTO-GML-0056 — The connection to Gmail was lost before the action finished

GUID: b547dcbb-aeb2-59e6-ad1b-dc6d5ef14770
Slug: gmail-imap-network-interrupted
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gmail_imap

What happened

  • SMTO's connection to Gmail broke, took too long, or was stopped while it was working. If the request was sending or changing mail, it may or may not have happened.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Gmail and look at Sent, Drafts, and the affected messages to see whether the send or change already went through. The connection ended before Gmail confirmed the result, so repeating it blindly could make a duplicate.
  2. Make sure the computer running the Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses to reach Gmail) is switched on and connected to the internet. Every Gmail action for this account travels through that computer's connection.
  3. If it keeps timing out, open More options › Parameter Store, select the Gmail account, and raise timeout_seconds in its Value tab (up to 120). Select Save. A longer wait gives Gmail more time to answer on slow networks or large mailboxes.
  4. Ask SMTO to test the Gmail connection, then ask only for the part that didn't happen. The test confirms the connection works again without changing any mail.

What success looks like

  • The Gmail connection test succeeds, and Gmail shows the action happened exactly once.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't repeat a send until you've checked Sent, and don't switch to a different account or sign-in method to get around this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The request-owned IMAP connection to imap.gmail.com failed, reached its min(300, timeout_seconds × 4) second deadline, or was cancelled before the operation returned a completion receipt.

What this means

  • The request-owned IMAP connection failed, reached its network deadline, or was cancelled. Confirmed substeps and effect_unknown remain authoritative. This diagnostic alone does not establish whether a prior write or send completed.

Why this can happen

  • Producer condition: The request-owned IMAP connection failed, reached its network deadline, or was cancelled.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact account revision, Gateway route and failing substep with the retained receipt.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the operation receipt and confirmed substeps first, and check Gmail for any write marked effect_unknown before repeating it. Restore network connectivity from the Gateway host to imap.gmail.com:993, or raise timeout_seconds (1–120) in the gmail_app_password_account parameter, before a new read or gmail.test_connection.
  • Inspect the operation receipt first. Preserve confirmed substeps and check Gmail before repeating a write whose result is unknown. Restore connectivity or adjust the saved network timeout before a new read or connection test.

Retry and execution caution

  • Preserve confirmed work and establish the current mailbox state before any repeated write.

How to verify the fix

  • The chosen operation completes with a matching receipt, or the remaining uncertain action is inspected in Gmail without duplicate mail.

What not to do

  • Do not switch accounts or authentication methods after failure, or automatically replay uncertain writes.

Technical notes

  • Confirmed substeps and effect_unknown remain authoritative. This diagnostic alone does not establish whether a prior write or send completed.
  • App-password setup: https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/185833
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
